claims.text: Co-doping an AlCoCrFeNi HEA coating with Y and Hf via laser cladding will improve the high-temperature oxidation resistance of zirconium-alloy nuclear-fuel cladding.
The Y/Hf-co-doped coating will retain suitability for service and will not compromise service compatibility.
Y and Hf act as reactive-element dopants in the HEA coating.
Introducing Y and Hf promotes formation of a more stable oxide scale.
Introducing Y and Hf promotes formation of a more adherent oxide scale.
Y/Hf addition modifies the microstructure and phase stability of the oxide layer.
Y/Hf co-doping produces finely dispersed secondary oxide phases during high-temperature exposure.
The secondary oxide phases enhance oxide-scale adhesion and integrity.
Improved oxide-scale adhesion and integrity mitigate spallation.
Y/Hf co-doping slows oxidation kinetics relative to the undoped AlCoCrFeNi coating.
The co-doped coating will have a lower oxide weight-gain rate than an undoped AlCoCrFeNi coating under identical high-temperature oxidation conditions.
The co-doped coating will have greater oxide-scale adhesion than the undoped coating.
The co-doped coating will delay the onset of oxide-scale spallation relative to the undoped coating.
The expected improvement is limited to temperature and duration ranges typical of reactor transient scenarios.
Performance may deviate at extreme temperatures, after exposure beyond tested durations, or when Y/Hf concentrations are substantially altered.
The optimal Y and Hf doping levels are uncertain.
Long-term stability under cyclic thermal conditions is uncertain.
